gettingStarted.lead: Get started with the APIs that are currently available, without needing to understand the internal implementation.
gettingStarted.tauri: Run AXION Core as a Tauri app on the same machine as the runtime running the AXION LocalScript. Vite alone does not provide the native WebSocket or HTTP listener.
gettingStarted.loadApi: Load lua/AXION api.lua in a Lua executor that supports WebSocket and the request function for localhost HTTP. The API connects to the WebSocket automatically by default.
gettingStarted.serverScript: To call a Server Script, save it on the Server Scripts page, use a scope matching CustomGameId in the client config, and copy the API token from that page.
gettingStarted.workflow: Call a Server Script from start to finish
gettingStarted.stepSave: In AXION Core > Server Scripts, enter the code below and save it. It exports the find_item function.
gettingStarted.stepScope: Set CustomGameId in the AXION API config to the selected scope. The scope does not need to match a specific game name.
gettingStarted.stepToken: Copy the API token from Server Scripts and replace the client-code placeholder. Treat the token as a secret; do not share it or include it in public source.
gettingStarted.stepInventory: An Agent must be connected and report inventory with AXION:ReportWorkspace before items can be searched.
gettingStarted.stepRun: Run the client code in an environment where the AXION API is loaded.
gettingStarted.runCode: 2. Run in the AXION LocalScript environment
gettingStarted.httpNote: This example requires a real token and reported inventory data. HTTP end-to-end cannot be tested without AXION Core, a runtime, and a token.
